comparator.name: Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 appendix defines a 150-ECTS Mathematics major and 30-ECTS minor. Year 1 is a compulsory 60-ECTS common Mathematics/Applied Mathematics foundation, instantiated with First-year Project Mathematics because it directly represents the named degree. The second- and third-year major contributes 90 ECTS. Dynamical Systems and Algebraic Structures are selected as the first two options in their regulated choice group; Project Statistical Reasoning is selected as the first option in the subsequent group; and Project Systems Theory is the first listed eligible elective. These choices are fixed by official order independently of UCR fit. The genuine 30-ECTS minor remains open rather than being populated with invented courses.

exception.reason: The Groningen bachelor is a full disciplinary Mathematics degree. Its 150-ECTS major develops proof-based analysis, sets and numbers, graph theory, two courses in both calculus and linear algebra, probability, programming, mechanics and linear systems into group theory, topology, complex and functional analysis, multivariable analysis, geometry, partial differential equations, numerical analysis, dynamical systems, algebraic structures, specialist mathematical projects and a 15-ECTS Mathematics research project. UCR offers a useful six-course mathematics sequence plus programming, algorithms, data science and quantitative applications, but it does not provide the breadth, theoretical depth, proof progression or research spine required for a Mathematics bachelor. A UCR programme assembled from mathematics, computing and data science would be a coherent quantitative pathway, not a defensible substitute for the target degree.
exception.curriculumContext: The current formal regulations account for exactly 180 ECTS: a compulsory 60-ECTS first year, a 90-ECTS second- and third-year major, and 30 ECTS of genuine minor space. Restricted choices are instantiated through the named-degree project and neutral official-order tie-breaks. The public programme page corroborates the theoretical emphasis in algebra, topology, analysis, probability, number theory, dynamical systems and cryptography.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods covers foundational calculus, complex numbers, differential equations and introductory linear algebra; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics extend that base. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and DISCOMP311 Algorithms & Data Structures add computational problem-solving. The workbook also contains relevant content in DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISCOMP312 Advanced Algorithms and quantitative data/AI courses. It nevertheless contains no sustained proof-based sequence in real analysis, metric and topological spaces, group theory, complex analysis, functional analysis, geometry and algebraic structures; no graph-theory or sets-and-numbers foundation; no full pure-mathematics progression in dynamical systems, probability and measure, number theory or algebraic topology; and no equivalent 15-ECTS disciplinary research project. Several relevant advanced courses, including DISMATH213, DISMATH312 and DISCOMP312, have no planned term for the Fall 2026 cohort in the authoritative workbook. These gaps prevent an academically honest 24-course Mathematics closest match.
